subject.title: fix(irc): disconnect on oversized inbound lines

question: After an oversized inbound IRC record, should the account automatically reconnect under channel supervision, remain disconnected until operator recovery, or discard the record and continue?
rationale: The IRC wire limit is clear, but the protocol does not select OpenClaw's account-level recovery policy; unconditional closure can intentionally change availability for existing IRC setups.

options.title: Fail closed, then reconnect
options.body: Retain socket closure and prove that the IRC monitor exits into bounded supervised reconnect/backoff with an observable unhealthy status for repeated violations.

options.title: Accept terminal disconnection
options.body: Merge the parser as written with an explicit owner decision that one oversized record may leave the account offline until existing supervision or an operator restores it.

options.title: Discard and continue
options.body: Drop the oversized record without closing the socket, accepting the greater risk of stream desynchronization or continued hostile input in exchange for connection availability.

recommendation.title: Fail closed, then reconnect
recommendation.body: Retain socket closure and prove that the IRC monitor exits into bounded supervised reconnect/backoff with an observable unhealthy status for repeated violations.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history and documented IRC ownership make Vignesh the best available decision owner for this transport lifecycle choice.
